data.title: The 'authenticity' of Celine Dion: 'She appeals to the Boomers and the Zoomers'
data.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Nick Rees-Roberts, Professor of Media, Culture and Communication at the Sorbonne Nouvelle University, Paris. Her appeal lies in an unusual ability to bridge categories that contemporary celebrity and pop culture often keep separate: generations, languages, cultural hierarchies and even the apparent opposition between authenticity and carefully constructed stardom.

data.title: ‘I gave up my life to care for my father’: How 9/11 shaped a son’s sense of duty and life trajectory
data.description: Jean-Emile Jammine is pleased to welcome Alessandro Stravato, a witness to the attacks of September 11th. His testimony offers a deeply personal account. He witnessed firsthand the second plane strike the World Trade Center from Arthur Ashe Stadium. Stravato’s first instinct was not to interpret the historical significance, just find his father, who was working at City Hall.  He found him alive, covered in debris and soot, trekking dozens of blocks through Manhattan. And while his father did survive, his health seriously deteriorated over the years. By 2015, as Alessandro's dad was losing his battle with cancer, he told his son to "stay strong."

data.title: ‘We did what we had to do’: 25 years on, 9/11 first responder reflects on duty, survival and family
data.description: Jean-Emile Jammine is pleased to welcome LaZetta Duncan, Retired NYPD Detective, 9/11 First Responder. Duncan remembers Ground Zero not as a historical event frozen in time, but as living history whose consequences continue to unfold and evolve 25 years on. Her testimony traces a striking progression: from the confusion and urgency of the attacks, rescue and recovery, to the grim transformation of gathering human remains and evidence inside a burning toxic apocalyptic crime scene. And we now learn of the overwhelming health consequences borne by responders despite repeated assurances that the air quality posed no health threat.

data.title: The race to make AI safer

data.title: ‘I’ve never been more terrified!’ Carly Rae Jepsen on motherhood, stardom and her horniest album ever
data.description: Call Me Maybe made the singer-songwriter famous – but also confused. Who was she? Who was her music for? Fourteen years later, about to release the double album Day and Night, she finally has some answers Carly Rae Jepsen is as bubbly as ever as she comes down for breakfast at Manhattan’s Hotel Chelsea. She’s one of those pop princesses, like Kylie Minogue, whose voice and demeanour remain unchanged whatever the situation. And she feels at home at this New York landmark where, last year, she married the musician and producer Cole MGN. That a wedding at the Chelsea would need to be kept to about 100 people was an immediate selling point. “I loved that it was smaller,” she says. “It felt big to me! I didn’t even get time with all the people that were there.” We’re here to talk about her new album, though, which comes out 14 years after the song that made her world-famous. Born and raised in the city of Mission in British Columbia, Jepsen had come third on Canadian Idol in 2007, and then released a low-key folk album called Tug of War in 2008, before dropping Call Me Maybe four years later. It became the bestselling global single of 2012; her second album, Kiss, came out in the same year. Now, at the age of 40, she has six more studio albums under her belt. The latest, Day and Night, is her take on marriage and motherhood. And, in its own way – which is to say, a bit coy, a bit breathy – it might also be Jepsen’s horniest album to date. Continue reading...

data.title: The US right still paints Muslims as the ‘enemy’. But they are fighting for a brighter future for Americans | Nesrine Malik
data.description: Progressive politicians such as Zohran Mamdani offer answers to the bitter post-9/11 legacy of failures at home and abroad Twenty-five years after 9/11, two pieces of journalism, describing two different phenomena in contemporary New York, tell us a great deal about a city, and indeed a world, caught between two eras. In one, New York Magazine dives into “ Habibi City ”, a New York where a “cultural shift is underway, led by a generation of New Yorkers coming into its own”. This new generation is labelled as originating in “SWANA” – south-west Asia and north Africa, a region that “includes countries from Palestine to Iran to Sudan”. In the other, Vanity Fair describes calls for Zohran Mamdani to not attend the 9/11 memorial ceremony as partly founded in “inchoate, emotional” impulses, that see “the city’s first Muslim mayor as a stand-in for the 19 Muslims who hijacked four planes and turned them into deadly weapons, part of the ‘them’ who attacked ‘us’.” Together they capture what has changed over a generation, and what remains stubbornly the same. Members of a diaspora of Muslim background are indeed breaking through and accumulating, as New York Magazine says, “clout”. They are no longer simply a fixture of bodegas and halal carts, but of Saturday Night Live, upmarket dining, entertainment and politics too. Mamdani is both the expression of that cohort and the catalyst of its recognition as an emerging force. They care deeply for their local communities but also for those in Gaza and beyond. Continue reading...

data.title: End Times Fascism by Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor review – the fightback starts here
data.description: A sharp analysis of the damage wrought by the reckless super-rich, and progressive toolkit for repairing it The more power the radical rightwing nationalists of our age accrue, the greater the risk that their destructive brand of politics becomes normalised. We should not, for instance, regard it as normal that the man in charge of the world’s largest nuclear arsenal casually promises “a whole civilisation will die tonight”. We should not accept that history’s first trillionaire is allowed to spread racist conspiracy theories to a hitherto unimaginable extent. We should be alarmed that, here in the UK, a party tipped to lead a potential future government is trying to cruise to power in the slipstream of this international movement. In fact, we shouldn’t just be alarmed by such developments: we should stop them and urgently repair the damage already done. But how? And what is the nature of that damage? This bold, clarifying intervention from Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor provides some of the answers. “End times fascism” is their term for a convergence of interests that can broadly be understood as a response to the climate crisis. Faced with a world coming under unprecedented strain from environmental shocks and an unequal, resource-hungry economic system, today’s reactionaries are effectively saying: bring it on. Continue reading...

data.title: The desecration of DC: from a giant arch to a nuke-proof bunker, Trump’s legacy-building blingfest is an architectural atrocity
data.description: A bloated ballroom, a six-storey military HQ, a helipad-cum-cocktail patio, a gilded angel on a giant arch honouring himself … our architecture critic deplores the decorator-in-chief’s mutilation of Washington When you have a developer as US president, you might expect some zhooshing up of the capital. A few buildings renovated, maybe some parks replanted. But when you have a megalomaniac builder in charge, things can get out of hand. A decade ago, when Donald Trump was first elected, I asked what it might mean for the US to be led by a real estate tycoon whose career had left a trail of broken promises, angry buyers and endless lawsuits, with rules flouted, heritage trampled and the world pockmarked by a fleet of aspirational towers clad with a flimsy veneer of luxury. The answer is worse than I could have imagined. With the air of a nightmarish Hollywood sequel, Trump 2 has seen the president’s true architectural ambitions unleashed: The Blingpire Strikes Back. As America’s self-styled decorator-in-chief, Trump has not only overseen the gilded mutilation of the White House, but embarked on the Mar-a-Lagofication of Washington DC itself, applying his gold paintbrush to statuary, daubing ponds with flaking pool liner, and brewing plans for a colossal triumphal arch – all procured in a blizzard of no-bid contracts . And, in true dodgy salesman style, this programme of bauble-building is turning out to be a high-profile decoy for deeper damage being wrought elsewhere. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘But enough about you …’ How to survive in a world of monologuists, interrupters and trauma dumpers
data.description: Conversations are supposed to be two-sided – but all too often we come up against someone who’s passionately, exclusively in love with the sound of their own voice. Time to fight back … When I was in my early teens, I was often invited round to a schoolfriend’s house for dinner. Her family struck me as wildly progressive: they were Danish and indulged in all sorts of “out-there” activities – fondues, candle-making and, most terrifying of all, the talking stick. Before the meal was served, someone would retrieve the sacred broom handle and it would be passed around the table. You could speak only if you had possession of the stick. Despite it being the most stressful thing ever (it meant being in the spotlight, and then remembering to keep quiet the rest of the time), I now frequently yearn for a more convenient version of that stick. For example, I met a friend recently who I see infrequently but keep up with via voice notes. No sooner had we sat down than he launched into a long discourse about his new marathon training food plan. He only broke the flow to order an omelette: “Four egg whites, two yolks, is that possible?” (We were in my local greasy spoon, so the request was greeted with mirth.) When we left, 90 minutes later, he finally had the grace to turn to me and ask: “And how are things with you?” Walking home, I felt a mixture of disappointment and irritation. Had he always been so self-absorbed? So uninterested in anyone else? I couldn’t help wondering if our one-sided virtual updates had played a part in the problem. There is a name for this type of egocentric behaviour – “conversational narcissism”. Although it was coined by the sociologist Charles Derber in his 1979 book The Pursuit of Attention, the term seems more relevant than ever. “WhatsApp communication and voice notes are really a series of monologues,” says Charlotte Fox Weber, a psychotherapist. “In face-to-face situations, people are forgetting how to pause naturally, to make space to hear and listen. And people are chatting on the phone – an activity that at least requires turn-taking in a defined way – much less often.” A lot of our communication online can feel weirdly transactional, focused on logistics or niche WhatsApp groups. According to Tamu Thomas, a life coach and author, this has damaged the art of improvised conversation. “People have less capacity for meandering conversations that don’t have a purpose,” she says. “A good dialogue is a back-and-forth between two people discovering new things about each other, even if they have known each other for years. Because there are now so many different channels available to stay in touch, some people are confusing communication with connection.” Knowledge is power, though. If you can recognise the five types of common conversation hogger, it will be much easier to handle them. Continue reading...

data.title: Israel accused of trying to ‘eliminate’ living conditions for Palestinians in West Bank
data.description: Report by Israeli human rights group says systematic and broad assault being waged on conditions required for Palestinians’ existence Israel is working towards the systematic “elimination” of the conditions that sustain Palestinian collective life in the occupied West Bank, according to a major report published by the human rights group B’Tselem. The Israeli organisation’s hard-hitting report, shared with the Guardian in advance of publication, says Israel is “dramatically intensifying its attacks on every aspect of Palestinian life in the West Bank”, including “the ability to get to work, take children to school or university, receive medical treatment or municipal services, meet family and friends, cultivate land or go on vacation … routine activities that make up human life”. 1,107 Number of Palestinians killed by Israel in the West Bank since October 2023 Continue reading...

data.title: Burrata and beyond: a foodie tour of northern Puglia, Italy
data.description: It’s the birthplace of the popular cheese, but the Barletta-Andria-Trani province in southern Italy has an array of local delicacies – from olive oil and yellow tomatoes to goat prosciutto ‘I don’t eat mozzarella outside Puglia,” says our friend Savio. “It’s not the same.” Savio is a very opinionated foodie, so I take his words with a pinch of good Puglian sea salt (see below). He was adamant about the superiority of the stretched-curd cheese from his home turf. Puglia is also the birthplace of ingredient du jour burrata, which originated in Andria, a few miles from Savio’s home town of Barletta. Andria forms one part of the triangular Barletta-Andria-Trani (BAT) province, often passed over for better-known parts of Puglia, despite the cheese connection and Barletta having miles of palm-backed, sandy beaches. Continue reading...

data.title: A spoonful of sugar: how South Africa’s weigh-and-pay shops are tackling ‘poverty tax’ head on
data.description: Run by a social enterprise, the six shops operate from shipping containers across Johannesburg’s Alexandra township and sell food and household goods by weight in small, affordable amounts Every morning, on her way to the laundry shop she runs in Johannesburg’s Alexandra township, Tsholofelo Mphela stops at a bright yellow shipping container to buy a few spoonfuls of sugar. Inside, shelves are lined with large jars of beans, rice and maize meal, and clear boxes filled with breakfast cereal and loose teabags. A tap dispenses cooking oil by the millilitre. The cashier weighs Mphela’s purchase before ringing it up for a few rand. Continue reading...

data.title: The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd review – Amanda Seyfried compels in wrenching prison drama
data.description: Toronto film festival: Tim Blake Nelson writes and directs a challenging, and unsettling, look at empathy and forgiveness that strikes a haunting note There are troubling questions posed in Tim Blake Nelson’s effectively glum prison drama The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd, a film that will rank among the most overwhelmingly feel-awful experiences of this year’s Toronto film festival . It’s a story told in a disarmingly folksy manner with plucked guitar strings and down south homespun wisdom before it quietly reveals itself to be about something far more serious and startling, elements of an escape thriller but mostly an unsettling moral drama. It’s likely to upset and enrage some but even those who might feel offended will at least feel something , a quality not to be sniffed at during a festival that can often pick politeness over provocation. It’s the new film from actor turned writer-director Nelson, whose work has often tended to confront and dissect difficult issues. He went to Auschwitz in The Grey Zone, transported Shakespearean tragedy to high school in O, and handled both rape and suicide in his debut Eye of God. It’s a fine line between grimness for the sake of grimness and being unwilling to shy away from grimness, and at times I wondered whether I was being overly prodded, whether certain scenes were bordering on exploitative. I left rattled by what I’d seen and what I was being forced to reckon with, but I think Nelson just about justifies himself and how far he goes partly because he does, in crucial moments, avoid showing more than is needed. The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd is premiering at the Toronto film festival and is seeking distribution Continue reading...

data.title: Alexander Zverev claims first US Open after four-set battle with Ben Shelton
data.description: No 1 seed wins 6-3, 7-6 (2), 5-7, 6-2 American’s hopes dashed in tense final For a passing moment at the end of a rugged third set, hope sprung anew for Ben Shelton. He had been outserved and outplayed for nearly three hours, but at 6-5 in the third set, one game from defeat, the American finally broke through. He burst into the return game finally pounding his forehand freely and he willed himself into an unexpected fourth set. After he had finished pumping his fist, cupping his ear to the crowd and admirably trying to initiate a drastic momentum shift, the next sequence was most revealing. Shelton opened the fourth set with a shaky game, immediately losing his serve at the start of the set. He worked hard until the end, but he was beaten by Zverev, the top seed, who closed out a 6-3, 7-6 (2), 5-7, 6-2 victory to lift his second grand slam title of the year. Continue reading...

data.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
data.description: Controversy rules the Manchester derby, Coventry get dunked on and Tottenham still can’t score a goal The 199th Manchester derby was defined by two controversial refereeing decisions: Phil Foden’s first-half red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes, and the VAR intervention to award Erling Haaland’s winning goal despite Enzo Fernández appearing to interfere with play from an offside position. In both cases, a healthy dose of common sense might have led to a different outcome – and Pro Ref later admitted that Haaland’s goal should not have stood. Still, it’s tough to argue that the final result was harsh on United. Foden’s dismissal gave the hosts a huge opportunity they failed to take, their best chance falling to Bryan Mbeumo in stoppage time. Michael Carrick began his reign with a 2-0 home derby win against 11 men in January, so this felt like a backwards step for the manager, unable to find a way to control the game. Carrick also bemoaned City’s two days of extra rest after Champions League games this week – but chose to keep Fernandes and others on for 90 minutes in the 4-0 stroll past Sabah. United’s next two league games are away at Fulham and at home to Spurs. Carrick will need to be smarter to stop an early-season wobble becoming something more serious. Niall McVeigh Match report: Manchester United 0-1 Manchester City Match report: Coventry 0-5 Brighton Match report: Sunderland 0-2 Arsenal Continue reading...

data.title: ‘An error of judgement’: Pro Ref admits mistake in awarding Haaland’s derby winner
data.description: Officiating body announces it will review the incident Unhappy Carrick says error was ‘as obvious as it gets’ Pro Ref admitted Erling Haaland’s winner in Sunday’s Manchester derby should not have been allowed after the video assistant referee ruled Enzo Fernández was not interfering with play in the build-up. The elite officiating body will review the decision and has contacted Manchester United. Haaland’s 60th minute goal for Manchester City at Old Trafford was initially ruled offside before the VAR’s intervention. It came after Josko Gvardiol’s cross hit Patrick Dorgu’s boot, passed Fernández and the United defender Lisandro Martínez, and was finished by the City No 9. VAR decided Fernández was not interfering despite Martínez marking the midfielder. Continue reading...

data.title: Europe win Solheim Cup against USA to give captain Anna Nordqvist last laugh
data.description: Europe beat USA 15-13 after 7-5 win in singles matches Lottie Woad seals victory with putt against Auston Kim Eyebrows were raised when Anna Nordqvist somewhat abruptly announced her retirement from competitive golf last month at the age of just 39. Heads were turned when Nordqvist kept Solheim Cup faith with the pairing of Charley Hull and Lottie Woad despite a miserable points return in the Netherlands. Nordqvist sounded unsure about elements of the Solheim Cup’s captains’ agreement before a ball was whacked in anger. The last laugh belongs to the Swede herself, who can sail off into the sunset having added a triumphant Solheim Cup captaincy to a career that had already returned three major wins. What a rousing afternoon this soon became for women’s golf in Europe. The understated Nordqvist was on the podium once more. Continue reading...

data.title: Ludek Miklosko, former West Ham and QPR goalkeeper, dies aged 64
data.description: Miklosko played 373 times for West Ham from 1990 He won 42 international caps from 1982 The former West Ham and QPR goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko has died at the age of 64. Miklosko, who won caps for Czechoslovakia and the Czech Republic, had been living with cancer. Miklosko joined West Ham from Baník Ostrava in 1990 for £300,000 after a trial and helped the club win promotion to the top division in his first season. He left in 1998 having made 373 appearances, joining QPR, initially on loan. Continue reading...

data.title: The Josh Allen rollercoaster is up and running again for the new NFL season
data.description: The Bills quarterback produced his usual thrills: a galloping touchdown run, a near game-ending mistake and a brilliant throw. Buffalo fans better hold on Having Josh Allen as your quarterback is a bit like owning a high-performance sports car with an odd mechanical flaw that can’t be repaired. Most of the results are amazing – perhaps unprecedented – but there are also times when you wonder if a safer ride would get you farther. In Buffalo’s 36-31 Sunday win over the Houston Texans, Bills fans saw all sides of the Allenmobile. The quarterback completed 20 of 29 passes for 334 yards, two touchdowns, no interceptions, and a passer rating of 130.5. He also ran the ball six times for 23 yards and two more touchdowns, the first a typical romp through the opposing defense . Continue reading...

data.title: Josh Kerr bags $150,000 for 1500m victory at Ultimate Championship
data.description: Scot wins with ease ahead of Nuguse and Myers Henrich’s final leg earns Britain silver in mixed relay Throughout Josh Kerr’s perfect season, he has made the sublime look routine. So when the bell rang for the final lap of the men’s Ultimate 1500m final, with the Scot in third and closing on the leader, Yared Nuguse, the next 53 seconds felt preordained. So it proved. First Kerr sauntered past Robert Farken into second. Then with 250m remaining, he scootered past Nuguse. The 20‑year‑old Australian star Cam Myers chased valiantly but Kerr smoothly nursed a three-metre lead to the finish. Continue reading...

So when the bell rang for the final lap of the men’s Ultimate 1500m final, with the Scot in third and closing on the leader, Yared Nuguse, the next 53 seconds felt preordained. So it proved. First Kerr sauntered past Robert Farken into second. Then with 250m remaining, he scootered past Nuguse. The 20‑year‑old Australian star Cam Myers chased valiantly but Kerr smoothly nursed a three-metre lead to the finish. Continue reading...

data.title: Enric Mas reigns supreme at last in Vuelta a España to delight Spanish fans
data.description: Mas wins title after three second-place finishes Tobias Johannessen takes final stage in Granada Spain’s Enric Mas secured his first Vuelta a España title on Sunday as Tobias Johannessen won the 21st and final stage in Granada, bringing the three-week Grand Tour to a close. The 31-year-old, who took the red jersey after Tadej Pogacar abandoned the race after a crash on stage eight, held off the four-time champion Primoz Roglic to become the first Spaniard to win the Vuelta since Alberto Contador in 2014. data.title: We greet the news that AI could extinguish us with a glazed indifference. What is the way out of this nihilism? | Brigid Delaney
data.description: There are several answers, and none of them will be provided by tech. One thing we must do is identify the ingredients for human flourishing To imagine the future as being almost entirely bleak has somehow crept into the collective this year. Last week I was having coffee with an old friend. He was telling me about what his kids wanted to study when they went to university, when he suddenly broke off, stared into the middle distance and said, “I wish I never had children.” Continue reading...

data.title: Freedom-loving Britain was at the heart of the 18th century slave trade – and this register proves it | William Pettigrew
data.description: Register of British Slave Traders reveals how deeply the trafficking of Africans was embedded in the country’s politics, economy, institutions and culture Two obstacles have prevented us from appreciating the significance of the slave trade in British history. The first arose from the abolition campaign, which finally overcame opposition in parliament in 1807. The abolitionists promoted the idea that opposition to the slave trade flowed naturally from British values: justice, freedom and Christian benevolence. The success of this strategy obscured the role those same British values had played in supporting the trafficking. Today, Britain’s leaders place abolition in the pantheon of great and definitive national moments. The second obstacle has been the ingrained tendency of the British to offshore the causes and effects of African chattel slavery to the Americas. According to this view, slavery, and the racial thinking it engendered, was an American, not European concern. But Europeans transported the great majority of enslaved African people to the Americas and reaped huge advantages from doing so. These advantages reshaped European societies. Continue reading...

data.title: Who better to defend Reform’s latest millions than Honest Bob Jenrick? | John Crace
data.description: The man who once helped Richard ‘Dirty’ Desmond save a load of tax was wheeled out to face Laura Kuenssberg You wait years for one party donation of £36m and then two come along at once . Reform can hardly believe its luck. All hail the crypto billionaires. Tacky pale turquoise suits all round. And Nigel Farage won’t have to worry about spending any of his own money – if you can call the £5m freebie his own money – on his security. Nor do those champagne and oyster lunches to discuss loose change donations of £500k from people living overseas pay for themselves. From now on Reform won’t need to bother getting out of bed for anything less than eight figures. Fair to say that if it had been Labour or the Tories trousering £72m from Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo then Reform would be on full outrage rampage. How the political system was rigged against it and how the two main parties are hotwired cash machines. In bed with the super-rich. But since the money is heading towards its own bank account, everyone in the party is totally chilled. This is just the way life ought to be. Who wouldn’t want a country where two billionaires can attempt to buy the democratic process? Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on the government’s corporate reforms: entrenching neoliberalism, not ending it | Editorial
data.description: A recent consultation on corporate reporting prizes the interests of shareholders over society. It’s a step in the wrong direction The question of what corporations are for is deeply political. In a 1970 article for the New York Times, Milton Friedman argued that the “social responsibility of business is to increase its profits”. The idea that CEOs should worry about providing good jobs was “pure and unadulterated socialism”, he wrote. Friedman and his fellow neoliberals saw companies as vehicles for enforcing their politics. Their ideas endured: UK bosses are now paid 130 times more than average workers. Despite Andy Burnham’s pledge to end neoliberalism, a 12-week consultation recently launched by his government risks entrenching it. The consultation was first announced as part of the Starmer government’s crusade against “red tape”. The average annual report for some businesses now runs to 98,000 words, and no doubt there are areas that could be simplified. But the consultation proposes removing vital information and presumes that company reports primarily serve shareholders, rather than other stakeholders. Both are steps in the wrong direction. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on Russian parliamentary elections: glimpses of weakness behind the facade | Editorial
data.description: The Kremlin’s clumsy efforts to engineer the outcome reveal growing anxiety about the public mood and a war that is failing Vladimir Putin’s authoritarian powers are not constrained by elections, but he is alert to the danger that his rule would look illegitimate without them. That creates a tension, which is resolved through “managed democracy” – a euphemism for fraud and repression camouflaged with ritual ballots, held under a constitution that notionally guarantees political freedoms but in reality serves only the president. Russians are invited to elect a new Duma, the lower chamber of parliament, later this week, but they know in advance that United Russia, the official party of Putinism, will win a majority . Continue reading...

data.title: The bird that changed Ecuador: how a chance discovery of a rare species helped to save many more
data.description: Thirty years after a US ornithologist first sighted a jocotoco antpitta, the foundation he set up to restore biodiversity is a model for conservation globally I have to confess that I rarely enjoy birding in montane cloud forests. The birds that live in these mountainous, cool and humid habitats are masters of disguise, usually passing themselves off as a leaf or other form of foliage. But if I want to see antpittas – elusive, ground-dwelling birds that rarely show themselves – then I have no choice. So, on a cool, cloudy morning my guide, Juan Carlos Crespo, Fredy Ramón Castillo, a local ranger, and I are standing on a steep, muddy path close to Tapichalaca Lodge, 2,500 metres above sea level in the eastern Andes, waiting for the jocotoco antpitta to emerge from the undergrowth. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Spraying should be the last option’: how farmers are exploring alternatives to pesticides
data.description: When pesticide proved no match for the insect, desperate Phyllis Nvuda tried a new way to save her infested orchard For two decades, Phyllis Nduva, 72, has grown mangoes and citrus in Wote, a town in Kenya’s eastern Makueni County. In the beginning, she only had to worry about ordinary fruit flies. She handled them simply, buying chemical pesticides and spraying her trees whenever they appeared. But then, in 2014, the false codling moth turned up on her farm. The small brown creature had been causing havoc in South Africa for years, and in 2007 it was spotted in Kenya. data.title: Farewell to Eden by Sebastian Faulks review – conflict and compromise, from a veteran of the genre
data.description: A returning British soldier is haunted by his time in Palestine in this panoramic epic set after the second world war Sebastian Faulks’s latest book focuses on the most irreconcilable geopolitical struggle of our age, the Israel-Palestine conflict. While “the sound of mortar and machine gun, the collision of flesh and metal” are integral to Faulks’s best known works, such as Birdsong, in his 17th novel the military presence is a peacekeeping one. It’s 1946 and infantry officer Philip Deval, who saw action in Normandy, is deployed to the Holy Land to take part in maintaining Britain’s mandate in Palestine. Initially Philip is second in command of a battalion overseeing febrile relationships between Jewish and Arab communities. Britain’s profound failures and manipulation in the region, and the imminence of its disastrous departure from the territory, come under scrutiny. While able to drum up motivation and cheer for the men in his battalions, privately Philip wrestles with inner melancholy. He is “shrouded” in a “loneliness … that insulates him from the world”. Experiences on the battlefield and other, slowly elucidated tragedies have led to his pessimistic bent. Much of what Philip observes in the Middle East, and his “foreboding” sense of its intractable problems, only confirms his despairing sense of human nature. It also underlines his ambivalence towards notions of divine benevolence. Continue reading...

data.title: We Are Family: photography from Images Vevey 2026 – picture essay
data.description: We visited the idyllic Swiss lakeside town of Vevey for its 10th Biennale of photography. Global head of photography Fiona Shields picks out some of her favourite projects on display Discover the 50 artworks on display at the 10th edition of the Biennale Images Vevey , 5-27 September 2026 Every two years, on the shores of Lake Geneva at the foot of the Swiss Alps, the town of Vevey transforms its public spaces and buildings with 50 installations of artistic projects from 21 countries, which are free and open to the public. With such a breathtaking natural setting as its backdrop, the photography displayed at Images Vevey has to strike its own particular note of magnificence to hold the gaze. Rising six storeys high, Sian Davey’s portrait of the renowned photographer Martin Parr, who died at the end of last year, sets the tone for this year’s festival. Taken in a splendid garden that seems to have flourished straight from Eden, the monumental portrait overlooks the town. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I never pass up a rewatch’: why Valley Girl is my feelgood movie
data.description: The latest in our series of writers explaining their most rewatched comfort films brings us back to 1980s LA As a teenager growing up in the 1990s, I was deeply obsessed with all things 1980s pop culture. Chalk it up to nostalgia for my Care Bears-filled childhood – or a stubborn adolescent desire to separate myself from the Dave Matthews Band-loving, khaki-wearing kids at my high school. (Mission accomplished: it’s safe to say I was the only person I knew rocking a bandana tied around my pants leg or a Wild Boys-era Duran Duran shirt.) Back then, I was especially drawn to 1980s teen movies. In my own life, I was having zero luck finding a New Romantic Romeo; instead, I pined after artsy, sensitive boys who didn’t know I existed. But throughout these films, even the most awkward characters managed to find a happy ending, with the ultimate examples being Samantha (Molly Ringwald) in Sixteen Candles landing hunky Jake Ryan or Stacy (Jennifer Jason Leigh) linking up with Rat (Brian Backer) in Fast Times at Ridgemont High. data.title: Goody Goody review – intriguing natural childbirth horror lurches into demonic occult blowout
data.description: After Samantha Robinson decides a forest cabin in deep winter is the perfect spot to bear her child, it’s going to be a very bad shift for the doula and midwife Conception, pregnancy and childbirth are defining human experiences, and so remain perennial themes for horror, from Rosemary’s Baby to the Alien franchise to Prevenge . Occupying a no-woman’s-land between life and death, they’re innately anxiety-inducing, perhaps making it harder for film-makers to supply a truly individual take. Debut director Raymond Creamer comes close by initially digging into the interpersonal dynamics around the home-birthing pool of a headstrong mother-to-be, before he defaults into a schlocky creature feature. Goody (Samantha Robinson) is in the pool, ready for battle, soaking in good vibes beamed at her by husband Jayson (Colby Hollman), his doula sister Candace (Zoe Renee) and their rock, midwife Sarah (Colleen Foy). But shaken by weirdly spaced contractions, Sarah takes Jason aside and admits that she has a bad feeling. It’s not purely premonition: a flashback reveals, in contrast to the new-age love-in around the tub, Goody’s insistence against Sarah’s advice that she give birth in winter at their forest cabin. The midwife fears it will make going to hospital too difficult should anything go wrong – and only agrees to supervise because Goody will probably go ahead solo if she pulls out. Continue reading...

data.title: Lenore review – incel’s obsession with online influencer turns into anatomy of dislocated digital-age mindset
data.description: Digital-age Australian psychodrama tracks the shut-in mania of dangerously disaffected male fan, but doesn’t get inside his mind If the parasocial phenomenon is a kind of hell, then Max Wren, protagonist of this Australian digital-age psychodrama, resides in the ninth circle. Self-barricading in a basement room surrounded by screens, working on a documentary about the object of his disaffection (an enigmatic influencer called Lenore), this obsessive shut-in makes Eminem’s Stan look like the Dalai Lama. Touching on subjects including the attention economy, the male gaze, and incel isolation and misogyny, director David Ward feels both Max and Lenore’s pain. But his ungainly debut film doesn’t fully transcend its stage origins to capture the splintered headspace of the terminally online. Like films about fictional pop stars that feature unconvincing music, it doesn’t help that the quickfire résumé of Lenore’s career only half-conveys her magnetism. A one-time beauty influencer called Veronica Brand, she later graduates to more extreme performance art-type stunts, such as livestreaming her miscarriage; a move that, spliced without her knowledge into a children’s TV broadcast, forced her into hiding. But this performative vulnerability, including hints of her abusive dad, apparently won her legions of OnlyFans-style acolytes. Not just Max, but also his colleague Sam (Sam Macdonald), a brash interloper outraged to find he was nothing special to Lenore and who turns up at Max’s door offering exclusive footage of her. data.title: Love of Your Life review – Margaret Qualley eats, grieves and loves in Amazon’s transporting saga
data.description: Toronto film festival: the actor gives one of her best performances to date in a smoothly made globe-trotting drama of a woman’s life after the loss of her husband There’s a jump scare about 30 minutes into the glossy romantic drama Love of Your Life that’s about as effective as anything you’ll see in a horror movie this year. The film is focused on the life and loves of Maya (Margaret Qualley), a twentysomething Boston nurse who meet-cutes with the nerdy and idiosyncratic Felix (Gabriel Basso) during the purchase of a nightstand. We follow the initial giddy rush of their courting as they progress all the way to an impromptu wedding over the course of a few years, marked by Maya’s change in age announced in text. But just as we’re about to process the unsettling introduction of Felix using Chekhov’s inhaler, a news report interrupts the sunny tone. Spoiler: it’s March 2020. Continue reading...

data.title: Emily St John Mandel: ‘When half the electorate disagrees on basic reality, how do you come back from that?’
data.description: Her hit novel Station Eleven seemed to predict the pandemic, now the novelist is tackling the future of the US. She talks about chance, world-building and experiencing a ‘tiny bit’ of clairvoyance When Emily St John Mandel was a child she had a dream that would stay with her for decades. It was a nightmare in which “I was trying to find my dad in a crowd, and there were other people who looked like him but weren’t him”, she says. “It just kind of struck my imagination.” Forty-ish years later, Mandel’s seventh novel, Exit Party, opens with a gathering in Los Angeles, 2031, where bizarre things happen. Doubles of some guests appear. Someone else disappears altogether. The novel then alternates between two potential future Americas, one riven by the chaos of civil war, the other a surveillance state. Continue reading...

data.title: Stitching our warped reality together: a cartoonist and art critic take different approaches to the Bayeux tapestry
data.description: One Guardian contributor was tasked with creating a modern-day version of the medieval masterpiece, the other with reviewing the original. Both their visions proved terrifyingly pertinent. Here’s how they both tackled it Our journalists often draw connections between seemingly disparate issues or events to give people a fuller grasp of how things interrelate. But not every story can convey the scope and complexity of today’s algorithmically warped reality. One of the Guardian’s regular cartoonists has managed this feat by drawing inspiration from a medieval embroidery made almost 1,000 years ago. Edith Pritchett was asked by her editors on the Guardian’s Saturday magazine to draw a modern-day version of the Bayeux tapestry, the 11th-century artwork that has been capturing imaginations this month as it goes on public display in the UK for the first time since its creation. Her updated version was included as a pullout poster in the print edition of the Guardian last weekend and also published as a special scrollable digital feature . Continue reading...

data.title: Burning Man at 40: the once anarchic desert festival faces a midlife crisis
data.description: The subversive bacchanal for San Francisco’s eccentric underground is ageing out amid an influx of the super-rich Burning Man , the infamous arts festival in the Nevada desert, turned 40 this year, and it’s showing some distinct signs of middle age. It’s not just the tech billionaires who show up to party, the chartered flights straight to the desert or the HBO documentary about behind-the-scenes power struggles . The tens of thousands of people who assemble each year to create a tent city in the wilderness appear to be growing older, and it doesn’t seem that they’re being replaced by as many younger “burners”, as festival participants are called. data.title: Is it true that … having a hot drink will cool you down?
data.description: A warm cup of tea can trigger sweating and lower your body temperature, but only if you’re in an airy space Could a warm cup of tea really be the key to cooling down in hot weather? Or is that just something caffeine fiends tell themselves when they’re still working through a pot of coffee as the temperature hits 30C? Prof John Tregoning, the author of Live Forever? A Curious Scientist’s Guide to Wellness, Ageing and Death, says it depends on the circumstances. He points to the work of Australian scientist Prof Ollie Jay, who is a world leader in researching heat and how it balances out in your body. Continue reading...

data.title: Hot and sour, vegetarian mapo and in spicy sauce: Fuchsia Dunlop’s tofu recipes
data.description: Wobblesome, firm or silken, tofu is a star ingredient in Chinese cooking. These dishes show why In the west, tofu is often viewed as a substitute for meat, which may explain why firmer types that can be cut into chunks and fried or grilled like meat have become so ubiquitous. In China, however, where tofu has been eaten for at least 1,000 years, it isn’t a substitute for anything; it’s simply a protein-rich ingredient that forms part of most people’s diets, can be cooked with meat and fish, and comes in myriad forms, from the tender, wobbly tofu used to make Sichuanese mapo tofu to firm smoked tofu, sheets of tofu “skin” and the silken tofu that can be as soft as creme caramel. Many Chinese tofu recipes are so delicious that habitual meat-eaters will devour them as keenly as vegetarians. Continue reading...

data.title: AI will transform capitalism – but how?
data.description: Technology is going to drastically reshape the economy, and it’s within our power to decide what that looks like The idea that autonomous, thinking machines may one day destroy property, hierarchy and inequality is as old as western political thought. In Aristotle’s Politics, the philosopher cites a fantasy from the Iliad, in which machines begin to act independently of human direction, concluding: “If every tool could perform its own work when ordered, or by seeing what to do in advance … if thus shuttles wove and quills played harps of themselves, master-craftsmen would have no need of assistants and masters no need of slaves.” The dream that automation could inaugurate a classless society is also present in the writings of Karl Marx. In 1858 he imagined the replacement of intellectual property with “socialised knowledge”, which would merge into a “general intellect”, blowing the foundations of capitalism sky high. data.title: Readers reply: what have been the most prescient or accurate predictions of the future?
data.description: The long-running series in which readers answer other readers’ questions considers the art of soothsaying, prognostication and futurism This week’s question: What would be the most useful superpower? ‘Fingertip shopping will be one of the many homemakers’ conveniences. This video console will be channelled into the store of her choice …” I’ve always been fascinated by this 1967 video (not 1969, as the label says) which accurately foresaw the advent of online shopping, CCTV, fax/email and electronic banking. (It was a little less prescient in its assumption of gender roles – wife shops, husband pays – but we’ll let that slide.) The video, entitled 1999AD, was made by the Philco-Ford company, an American electronics firm that started off in radios and moved into appliances and TVs. I’ve often wished the writer of this short film could see the world as it is in 2026. What are some other predictions that have come spookily close to the truth? Ann, Devon Send new questions to nq@theguardian.com . Continue reading...

data.description: The singer-songwriter on her rock’n’roll past, playing second fiddle to the Beatles, and the key to being an energetic performer in your 80s Born Elaine Bookbinder in Salford in 1945, Elkie Brooks is a rock, blues and jazz singer known as the British Queen of Blues. She spent much of the 1960s on the cabaret circuit, during which time she supported the Beatles. She joined Dada in 1970, before forming Vinegar Joe with Robert Palmer in 1971. She went solo after their split, breaking through with Pearl’s a Singer and Sunshine After the Rain, scoring 13 UK Top 75 singles. A celebration of six decades in music, The Long Farewell Tour, is now on the road. This is me in a white jumpsuit outside the Royal Albert Hall in London. I have very few memories of the gig, but I know I would have felt daunted as it’s such a large venue. To overcome the nerves, I’d have tried to focus on the music and remembered, “It’s just another gig.” Continue reading...

data.title: In 1869, 100 sheep became 5,000 on Socorro Island; 1,762 removed as forest-habitat vegetation cover rose 29%-85%
data.description: Feral sheep introduced to Socorro Island caused severe ecological damage over decades.  An eradication program removed 1,762 sheep between 2009 and 2012.  Vegetation cover and soil conditions began recovering surprisingly quickly after grazing pressure ceased.  This recovery demonstrated the island's remarkable ecological resilience and capacity for self-repair.  However, other invasive species like feral cats remain a significant conservation challenge.

data.title: How Singapore turned garbage ash into a 350-hectare island where mangroves and coral now flourish
data.description: Singapore has pioneered a remarkable 350-hectare landfill created from incinerated waste, known as Semakau Landfill. With migratory birds nesting and corals thriving, this man-made island exemplifies successful waste management, projected to remain operational until 2035.

data.description: After a dramatic 150-year absence, conservationists have triumphantly reintroduced ospreys to England. Young chicks, sourced from Scotland, began their journey to Rutland Water in 1996. Remarkably, these avian travelers instinctively returned to their new home, initiating a breeding cycle that has led to over 300 fledglings now populating the area. This successful initiative marks a pivotal moment in conservation efforts.

data.title: 28 unseen Andy Warhol digital artworks from 1985 recovered from old Amiga floppy disks
data.description: In 1985, Andy Warhol experimented with digital art on an Amiga computer for a Commodore International commission. Nearly 30 years later, researchers recovered 28 previously unseen images from ageing floppy disks at The Andy Warhol Museum. The files had been trapped in an obsolete format and included works featuring Campbell’s soup cans, Venus, Marilyn Monroe and self-portraits.

data.title: Etiópia recebe primeiro escritório africano da ApexBrasil
data.description: Na última sexta-feira (11), começou 2019 na Etiópia . Em 11 de setembro, etíopes comemoraram o Enkutatash, seu Ano-Novo. País de antiga tradição cristã, que remonta ao Reino de Axum no século 4, nunca colonizado apesar das duas tentativas italianas, uma no século 19 e outra de Mussolini, o calendário etíope tem 13 meses, 12 deles com 30 dias e um último, com 5 ou 6. A diferença em relação ao calendário gregoriano, por nós utilizado, vem de cálculo da cronologia cristã. A vida cotidiana segue o calendário etíope, o ciclo diário começa ao amanhecer, não à meia noite, o amárico, língua de trabalho do governo em um país multilíngue, é escrito no fidel etíope, sistema de escrita derivado do ge'ez. Leia mais (09/13/2026 - 23h00)

data.title: Tomas Ramberg: Blir Åkesson eller Andersson valets största förlorare?
data.description: Riksdagsvalet 2026 blev tidernas nagelbitare. Nu famlar det politiska Sverige i väntan på att den slutliga rösträkningen blir klar på onsdag. Men redan nu står det klart att Socialdemokraterna och Sverigedemokraterna är valets stora förlorare. Om oppositionens övertag står sig är det ett grundskott mot Sverigedemokraternas ställning i svensk politik. Men skulle Tidöpartierna stå som slutsegrare väntar räfst och rättarting i Socialdemokraterna.

Samtidigt börjar det stå klart att Liberalerna har klarat spärren med marginal. – Det här valresultatet kan leda till en komplicerad regeringsbildning, säger M-ledaren Ulf Kristersson.

data.title: Rekordmånga har röstat tidigt i utsatta områden: ”En gåva från Allah”
data.description: Rekordmånga har förtidsröstat i årets val. Ökningen är störst i särskilt utsatta områden. 71 procent fler hade på söndagen förtidsröstat jämfört med föregående val, enligt DN:s sammanställning. I Angereds moské slår man fast att rösträtten är ”en gåva från Allah”. – Det kan gynna Socialdemokraterna, säger Zeth Isaksson, forskare vid Stockholms universitet.

data.title: AI-jättarna varnar själva för domedagen – bara Trump tycks obekymrad
data.description: NEW YORK. När cheferna för AI-jättar som Anthropic och Open AI själva varnar för domedagen ställer sig hela USA frågan: Håller vi på att skapa ett monster? data.title: Historiskt toppmöte: Skottland, Wales och Nordirland enas mot London – vill bli självständiga
data.description: I morgon måndag möts ledarna för Skottland, Wales och Nordirland. Mötet beskrivs som unikt – det är första gången alla tre riksdelarna leds av nationalistiska partier som förespråkar självständighet från Storbritannien. Syftet med toppmötet är att teckna ett gemensamt avtal för att tvinga fram folkomröstningar om saken – något som premiärminister Andy Burnham hävdar saknar folkligt stöd.

data.title: Nauka potrzebuje przewidywalności
data.description: Najważniejszy wniosek z naszej debaty jest jasny: naukę należy traktować jako długofalową inwestycję państwa. Uczelnie kształcą kadry dla gospodarki, prowadzą badania i tworzą technologie potrzebne do mierzenia się z wyzwaniami, których skali i charakteru nie potrafimy dziś przewidzieć. Rolą uczelni jest nie tylko nadążanie za zmieniającym się światem, lecz także współtworzenie jego przyszłości. Dyskusja o finansowaniu uczelni zbyt często sprowadza się do wyboru między subwencją a grantami. Potrzebujemy jednak trzech uzupełniających się kanałów: stabilnej subwencji, sprawnego krajowego systemu grantowego oraz strategicznych inwestycji państwa.

data.title: W Gdańsku powstaje nowy gigant. Ruszyła budowa „Big Boya”
data.description: Na mapie Gdańska wkrótce pojawi się nowy, imponujący punkt orientacyjny. Rozpoczęła się budowa wieżowca o nazwie „Big Boy”, który ma mieć 99 metrów wysokości. Budynek powstanie na Przymorzu Wielkim. Ruszyły już pierwsze prace ziemne i geotechniczne.

data.title: Rekordowa emerytura w Polsce. ZUS wypłaca ponad 54 tys. zł miesięcznie
data.description: Najzamożniejszy polski emeryt otrzymuje 54 tys. 72 zł miesięcznie i mieszka w województwie śląskim. Także drugą co do wysokości emeryturę – 53,5 tys. zł – otrzymuje mieszkaniec Śląska. Podium zamyka osoba z woj. mazowieckiego, która co miesiąc dostaje 45,3 tys. zł – poinformował Zakład Ubezpieczeń Społecznych.

data.title: Hvězdy StarDance roztančí parket již po čtrnácté. Co všechno je letos čeká?

data.title: Do srážky osobních vlaků chybělo málo, zasáhl generální stop. Případ řeší policie
data.description: Bezpečnostní systém „generální stop“ zabránil tragédii na železniční trati mezi Pískem a Táborem. Zastavil dva vlaky jedoucí proti sobě, když jeden ze strojvedoucích pravděpodobně přehlédl návěstní světelný zákaz a vyjel ze stanice. Případem se zabývají kriminalisté pro podezření ze spáchání trestného činu obecné ohrožení.

data.title: Vyrazili spolu na houby, měli se sejít u auta. Na Sokolovsku se ztratil houbař
data.description: Od neděle pátrá policie po dvaašedesátiletém Emilu Tkáčovi, který se ztratil při houbaření nedaleko Jindřichovic na Sokolovsku. Na houbách byl od dopoledne se svým kamarádem, který na policii ohlásil, že se muž ztratil. Policisté spolu s hasiči po muži pátrali, ale dosud jej nenalezli, řekla v pondělí ráno krajská policejní mluvčí Kateřina Pešková.

data.title: Vláda jedná o přitvrzení vůči kratomu. Bude možné si ho koupit až od 21 let
data.description: Přitvrdit vůči drogám se rozhodla vláda Andreje Babiše. Projednává novelu o návykových látkách, podle které bude možné koupit si od příštího roku v Česku kratom legálně až od 21 let. Dosud to bylo možné od 18 let. Ministryně financí za ANO Alena Schillerová také počítá s přeřazením kratomu do vyšší, základní sazby 21 procent.

data.title: Rychlostní limit ve městech? Pirátka Lněničková se opřela o zavádějící data
data.description: Zastánkyně rychlostního limitu 30 km/h ve městech, pražská pirátská zastupitelka Gabriela Lněničková, čelí kritice kvůli sdílenému příspěvku. Pozitivní dopady na bezpečnost a emise dokládala materiálem, který vychází ze zavádějících dat. Svůj komentář navíc doplnila o zcestnou mapu Evropy vygenerovanou umělou inteligencí.

data.title: Každá ruka dobrá. Rusové už mohou na frontě čerpat sílu z knížecích ostatků
data.description: Ruský prezident Vladimir Putin zaslal ruským jednotkám válčícím na Ukrajině neobvyklou posilu v podobě 637 let staré relikvie. K vojákům na Donbasu zamířila část nedávno nalezených ostatků Dmitrije Donského, středověkého knížete a světce pravoslavné církve. Zdobenou schránku s kusem ruky vozí zástupci ruského patriarchátu přímo mezi vojáky v první linii.

data.title: Těsný souboj o parlament ve Švédsku. Nacionalističtí Švédští demokraté oslabili
data.description: Středolevý opoziční blok podle aktualizovaných předběžných výsledků nedělních parlamentních voleb ve Švédsku získal 176 křesel, dosavadní vládní blok 173. Vyplývá to z projekcí švédského volebního úřadu. Nacionalističtí Švédští demokraté si oproti minulým volbám pohoršili, dosavadní výsledky jim přisuzují 17,6 procenta hlasů, o tři procenta méně než posledně.

data.title: Turek prohrál soud s Hnutím Duha, musí se omluvit za výrok o „parazitech“

data.title: Šef ŘSD: Potřebujeme i třetí okruh kolem Prahy, desítky kilometrů od metropole
data.description: Česko zažívá jeden z největších dálničních boomů ve své historii. Šéf ŘSD Radek Mátl v Rozstřelu promluvil o cenách dálnic, dostavbě Pražského okruhu i plánech na další dálniční síť. Praha podle něj bude v budoucnu potřebovat dokonce třetí, aglomerační okruh desítky kilometrů od metropole.

Šéf ŘSD Radek Mátl v Rozstřelu promluvil o cenách dálnic, dostavbě Pražského okruhu i plánech na další dálniční síť. Praha podle něj bude v budoucnu potřebovat dokonce třetí, aglomerační okruh desítky kilometrů od metropole.

data.title: Trump během golfového turnaje slíbil zrušení cla na irskou whiskey
data.description: Americký prezident Donald Trump slíbil, že Spojené státy zruší clo na dovoz irské whiskey. O jeho odstranění ho podle vlastních slov žádali mimo jiné i někteří golfisté během turnaje Irish Open. Irská whiskey nyní podléhá 15procentnímu clu, které Trump zavedl na dovoz z Evropské unie. Prezident neuvedl, kdy by mělo být clo zrušeno

data.title: Ukrajina musí přestat s útoky na ruské rafinerie, trvá na svém Trump
data.description: Americký prezident Donald Trump znovu prohlásil, že Ukrajina by neměla útočit na ruské rafinerie. Uvedl to v noci na pondělí při návratu z Irska do USA. Trump řekl, že vyzval ukrajinského prezidenta Volodymyra Zelenského, aby ukrajinská armáda neútočila na ruské ropné cíle, protože to „škodí celému světu“.

data.title: Motorkářce zkřížila cestu srna. Žena utrpěla vážné poranění nohy

data.title: IKEM porušoval zákony při nakládání s penězi. NKÚ našel desítky pochybení
data.description: Hospodaření IKEM má podle Nejvyššího kontrolního úřadu vážné nedostatky. Institut v letech 2022 až 2024 opakovaně porušoval zákony i vlastní pravidla při nakládání s veřejnými penězi a majetkem. Kontroloři našli pochybení u poloviny z 30 prověřovaných zakázek a upozornili také na případy, kdy IKEM zadával zakázky bez soutěže jedinému dodavateli.

data.title: Vojáci KLDR cvičili ostrými útok na nepřátele. Testovali drony, rakety i střely
data.description: Severní Korea otestovala při vojenském cvičení několik typů zbraní včetně útočných dronů, střel s plochou dráhou letu a balistických raket. Manévry měly podle severokorejské agentury KCNA posílit morálku vojáků a jejich schopnost zničit nepřítele na rozkaz. Cvičení se uskutečnilo krátce poté, co Pchjongjang odpálil několik balistických střel krátkého doletu do moře.

data.title: Volby 2026: kandidáti na primátory krajských měst. Komunální volby přehledně
data.description: Primátora a nové vedení radnic budou letos vybírat voliči v komunálních volbách ze 190 153 kandidátů. Největší výběr mají z velkých měst Pražané, kde do zastupitelstva hlavního města kandiduje 1 060 lidí na 24 listinách. Volby se uskuteční v pátek 9. a v sobotu 10. října 2026. Přinášíme přehled hlavních kandidátů na primátora v krajských městech.

data.title: Počasí ukáže dvě tváře. Teploty až 27 stupňů, pak přijde výrazná změna
data.description: Počasí v Česku bude v příštích dnech proměnlivé. Po slunečném a teplém úterý se od středy začne zatahovat a místy dorazí déšť, přeháňky a bouřky. Ve čtvrtek se výrazně ochladí a chladnější počasí vydrží i v závěru týdne. O víkendu bude převládat oblačná až polojasná obloha, místy se objeví přeháňky.

data.title: Bio versus regenerativní zemědělství. O půdu i peníze se povede velký boj
data.description: Rozpor mezi ekologickými a regenerativními zemědělci se prohlubuje, byť by obě cesty měly vést k udržitelnému hospodaření a lepší péči o půdu. Nejnovější spor vyvolala předsedkyně zemědělského výboru Evropského parlamentu Veronika Vrecionová (ODS), která navrhuje změny budoucích dotačních pravidel od roku 2028.

data.title: Eleições na Suécia. Resultados provisórios colocam esquerda no poder
data.description: O Partido Social-Democrata venceu as eleições parlamentares de domingo na Suécia. Os partidos da esquerda (que têm estado na oposição) lideram com uma vantagem mínima sobre os de direita, com quase 95 por cento dos votos apurados. Liderados pela antiga primeira-ministra sueca Magdalena Andersson, os social-democratas e mais três partidos de centro-esquerda conquistaram uma maioria frágil sobre o bloco de direita que governa os suecos.

data.title: Israeli minister calls for revocation of citizenship for directors over Gaza documentary
data.description: Israeli Culture and Sports Minister Miki Zohar on Sunday called for the revocation of citizenship for directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, whose documentary ‘NAZA’—depicting Israeli military actions in Gaza—received a special jury prize at the Venice Film Festival. Zohar, in a statement posted on X, accused the filmmakers of ‘treason against the state’ due to the film’s portrayal of AI-assisted military operations. The directors have not responded publicly, and the Ministry of Interior has not commented. International film and rights groups have criticized the move, citing concerns over freedom of expression.

data.title: What We Are Reading Today: ‘Into the Great Wide Ocean’ by Sonke Johnsen
data.description: The open ocean, far from the shore and miles above the seafloor, is a vast and formidable habitat that is home to the most abundant life on our planet, from giant squid and jellyfish to anglerfish with bioluminescent lures that draw prey into their toothy mouths. “Into the Great Wide Ocean” takes readers inside the peculiar world of the seagoing scientists who are providing tantalizing new insights into how the animals of the open ocean solve the problems of their existence.

data.title: Armando.Info: Con la muerte del Niño Guerrero, todo cambió para seguir igual en las minas
data.description: La operación militar conjunta del pasado junio entre fuerzas de Venezuela y Estados Unidos despertó expectativas de altos quilates en el sureste del estado Bolívar, una región aurífera hasta entonces sometida al yugo de las bandas criminales. Sin embargo, los eventos posteriores se quedaron cortos. Los habitantes de los asentamientos mineros de Las Claritas y Kilómetro 88, donde el Tren de Aragua se había hecho fuerte, apenas sienten mejoras, y ya empiezan a añorar el antiguo orden de los ‘pranes’ que todavía andan por allí. The post Armando.Info: Con la muerte del Niño Guerrero, todo cambió para seguir igual en las minas appeared first on EL NACIONAL .

data.title: Burundi : Sous la cloche de septembre, les jeunes talents ont chanté
data.description:
Ce samedi 12 septembre 2026, sous un ciel qui refusait l’indifférence, s’est refermée la dernière page d’un conte écrit avec des crampons et des rêves d’enfance. 
 Le Young Talent Challenge Trophy , ce tournoi qui conviait les pépinières du football burundais, celles qui façonnent les mollets de moins de quinze ans, a rendu son verdict. Et la poussière des terrains s’est faite encre pour graver des noms.

data.title: Ligue des Champions, CAF : Rideau sur le rêve d’Aigle Noir, Al-Hilal poursuit son chemin
data.description:
Les cieux de Kigali n’ont pas tremblé. Al-Hilal a fait ce qu’on attendait des grands : imposer sa loi, sans éclat inutile, mais avec une autorité glaciale.  
 Au terme d’une double confrontation maîtrisée de bout en bout, les Soudanais se sont offert une qualification nette pour le deuxième tour préliminaire de la Ligue des Champions de la CAF : 3-0 sur l’ensemble des deux matchs face à Aigle Noir CS.

data.title: États-Unis : L’Afrique du Sud veut empêcher la vente aux enchères de 29 objets historiques ayant appartenu à Nelson Mandela

data.title: Vincent Sosthène Fouda : « Le Cameroun a besoin de Kamto, pas de sa mort politique »
data.description: © DR Il a 53 ans, il a fait de la politique depuis les bancs de la fac, et il dit tout haut ce que beaucoup murmurent à la suite de la démission du Pr Maurice Kamto à la tête du MRC. Dans une tribune au ton très élevé, Vincent Sosthène Fouda prend le contre-pied du jeu politique actuel : faire de la chute de Maurice Kamto un projet. "Il faut le dire avec clarté, avec hauteur, avec sens de l'État : tuer politiquement Maurice Kamto ne saurait constituer un programme politique", lance-t-il. Pour lui, cette obsession révèle "une inquiétante pauvreté stratégique". Comme si après Kamto, le Cameroun allait miraculeusement s'arranger. Fouda balaie : "C’est confondre l’écume avec la mer." Son message est simple : la démocratie n'est pas un théâtre où on attend qu'un acteur sorte de scène. "C'est un chantier. Un effort. Une construction patiente." Et il liste les vraies urgences que le débat sur Kamto fait oublier : moderniser l'Etat, refonder le pacte social, casser la corruption systémique, restaurer la confiance, préparer la relève et intégrer le futur technologique. Sa phrase finale claque comme un manifeste : "La grandeur d’une Nation ne se mesure pas à la chute de ses adversaires, mais à la hauteur de ses projets. Pour cela, l’opposition et la vie politique camerounaise ont besoin de Maurice Kamto." Une prise de position qui intervient 5 jours après la lettre-choc du Pr Alain Fogue depuis Kondengui, qui lui aussi dénonçait la "kamtophobie d'Etat". Deux textes, deux hommes différents, même constat : on ne construira pas le Cameroun d'après-Biya sur la seule élimination de Kamto. En dehors de ces deux hommes politiques, d’autres acteurs de la scène politique national ont ait des sorties à la suite de la démission de Maurice Kamto à la présidence du MRC. Ce fond est presque le même du côté de Cet article Vincent Sosthène Fouda : « Le Cameroun a besoin de Kamto, pas de sa mort politique » est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : de Kondengui, Alain Fogue annonce un « génocide bamiléké programmé » et accuse le clan Biya de préparer la royauté
data.description: © DR Le Pr Alain Fogue dégaine une lettre-bombe de 8 pages. Il dit craindre un génocide, dénonce la création d'un Vice-Président successeur non élu et interpelle les présidents Paul Biya, Emmanuel Macron, Donald Trump ainsi que l'ONU. Le coup est venu de là où on ne l'attendait plus : la Prison Centrale de Kondengui. Le 2 septembre 2026, le Pr Alain Fogue Tedom, cerveau économique du Mouvement pour la Renaissance du Cameroun et prisonnier depuis 6 ans, a fait sortir une lettre ouverte explosive adressée à la planète entière. Les destinataires sont le président Paul Biya en personne, mais aussi l'Union africaine-UA, l'ONU, le président Emmanuel Macron à Paris, le president Donald Trump à Washington, Benyamin Netanyahou à Jérusalem, et même la Suisse et le Commonwealth. La correspondance porte sur la "Kamtophobie, bamiphobie". "On passe de la République à la royauté" Au cœur de sa charge, le fameux poste de vice-président de la République créé en avril 2026. Un vice-président qui sera nommé par Paul Biya, mais qui deviendrait automatiquement président en cas de vacance. Sans élection. Pour Fogue, c'est un coup d'Etat constitutionnel pur et simple. Il cite l'article 64 de la Constitution de 1996 : "aucune révision ne peut porter atteinte à la forme républicaine". Pour lui, c'est violé. Il appelle cela : "La succession de gré à gré, en famille, sans passer par les urnes".  Et il enfonce le clou : saisi fin avril, l'Union Africaine se tait. Un silence coupable, selon lui. "Le Cameroun, c'est le Rwanda de 1993" C'est la phrase qui va faire le tour du pays. Fogue écrit : "Le Cameroun d'aujourd'hui rappelle le Rwanda d'avant avril 1994". Il ressort le dossier qui fâche : la "guerre cachée" de 1955-1971. Il avance 400.000 morts Bamilékés, soit 37% de la communauté à l'époque, sur une population totale de 6,4 millions en 1970. Il pousse la comparaison jusqu'à la Shoah. La raison en est que, selon lui, les Bamilékés seraient aujourd'hui victimes d'un "apartheid politique". La preuve : "Jamais un Bamiléké ministre de la Défense depuis l'indépendance. Jamais un ministre des Finances, un chef d'état-major des armées, un chef d'état-major particulier sous Biya en 43 ans." Il ajoute que même à la banque ou à l'agro-industrie, on leur interdirait de racheter Société Générale ou la SOCUCAM. Kamto, l'ennemi intérieur Toute la lettre tourne autour de Maurice Kamto. Pour Fogue, la haine contre Kamto, c'est de la "kamtophobie" qui cache une "bamiphobie d'Etat". Il rappelle la présidentielle de 1992 perdue par Fru Ndi : "Les Bamilékés l'ont payé cher". Celle de 2018 : "On a déversé la haine du Bamiléké". Et celle de 2025 : candidature de Kamto rejetée le 5 août par le Conseil constitutionnel après un "acte de cybercriminalité sur le site du MINAT", selon lui. Il ressort la phrase de Jean du ministre délégué Dieu Momo le 4 février 2019 sur la CRTV : "En Allemagne, il y avait un peuple très riche... un jour Hitler les a mis dans les chambres à gaz... il faut que M. Kamto sache où il emmène son peuple". Fogue note : "7 ans après, il est toujours ministre". Un pays à genoux Le Pr Alain Fogue dresse un tableau noir : guerre anglophone depuis 2017, Boko Haram depuis 2014, crise post-électorale de 2025 avec "des dizaines de manifestants abattus à bout portant". Il cite l'assassinat de Martinez Zogo en janvier 2023, et l'inculpation du patron de la DGRE Léopold Maxime Eko Eko. Il interpelle la Suisse : "Biya a fait de l'Intercontinental de Genève son second palais". Et Israël : via son conseiller Eran Moas et sa "légion israélienne au cœur de la terreur d'Etat". Il dit être prêt à mourir Dernière ligne, glaciale : "Cette correspondance peut me coûter la vie. Mais je suis prêt, comme Um Nyobe et Ossende Afana, à être assassiné pour la LIBÉRATION du Peuple." Il aligne trois exigences : d’abord, qu’on supprime le poste de vice-président héritier. Ensuite, qu’on revient à la Constitution de 1996 ; que c'est le président du Sénat qui assure l'intérim 20 à 120 jours. Enfin, qu’on refasse tout le Code électoral avant toute élection. Agrégé d'économie, ancien trésorier national du MRC, Alain Fogue est en prison depuis la nuit du 21 au 22 septembre 2020. Condamné à 7 ans par le Tribunal militaire. L'ONU, via son Groupe sur la détention arbitraire (Avis 63/2022), a demandé sa libération. Yaoundé n'a jamais appliqué. Cet article Cameroun : de Kondengui, Alain Fogue annonce un « génocide bamiléké programmé » et accuse le clan Biya de préparer la royauté est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Des centaines d’hectares de cultures et de forêts détruits par des groupes armés à Masisi, selon la société civile
data.description: Des centaines d’hectares de reboisements et de bananeraies ont été détruits au cours des deux derniers mois sur plusieurs axes autour du chef-lieu du territoire de Masisi, au Nord-Kivu, alerte la société civile locale il y a quelques jours. Elle craint des conséquences sur l’environnement et l’approvisionnement alimentaire des populations.

data.title: La Synergie des syndicats des enseignants de la RDC suspend sa grève  mais dénonce la « démotivation » du personnel
data.description: La Synergie des syndicats des enseignants de la RDC suspend son mouvement de grève, tout en dénonçant la « démotivation » du personnel enseignant. La décision a été prise samedi 12 septembre à Kinshasa, à l’issue d’une assemblée générale d’évaluation du mouvement.

data.title: L’Inspection générale de la police contrôle les commissariats de Tshangu et de la Nsele à Kinshasa
data.description: L’Inspection générale de la Police nationale congolaise (IG-PNC) a lancé, vendredi 11 septembre, une mission de contrôle de trois jours dans les commissariats urbains de Tshangu et de la Nsele, à Kinshasa. Selon un communiqué de la police, cette opération vise notamment à vérifier le respect des droits humains, la protection des libertés publiques et la légalité des actes posés par les policiers.

data.title: Beni : : une vidéo des militaires au centre de concours d’admission dans les écoles militaires sortie de son contexte

data.title: Union européenne – Madagascar : un appui pour les réformes électorales
data.description: Jeudi soir à Bruxelles, le colonel Michaël Randrianirina a rencontré Kaja Kallas. Le chef de l'État malgache et la vice-présidente de la Commission européenne ont longuement parlé des élections. Le reste de la coopération n'a pas été oublié, mais le calendrier politique de la transition a dominé les échanges. L'Union européenne se dit prête à accompagner Madagascar. C'est ce qu'a réaffirmé Kaja Kallas. De son côté, le président de la Refondation a été clair : le pays a surtout besoin (…) - Coopération

Elle a notamment évoqué des procédures portant sur des soupçons de détournement de deniers publics et d'abus de pouvoir, mais également une affaire directement liée à la nationalité de l'ancien chef de l'État. Selon la ministre, la justice a été saisie afin d'enquêter sur l'utilisation par Andry Rajoelina (…) - Socio-politique

data.title: Madagascar-France : Randrianirina et Macron se retrouvent à l'Élysée
data.description: La rencontre a bel et bien eu lieu. Emmanuel Macron et le colonel Michaël Randrianirina se sont entretenus jeudi 10 septembre au palais de l'Élysée, à Paris. Le rendez-vous figurait officiellement à l'agenda du président français à 12 h 05, en marge du Sommet international sur l'espace. Au cœur des échanges : les relations entre Madagascar et la France et les perspectives de renforcement de la coopération bilatérale. Ce tête-à-tête constitue la deuxième rencontre entre les deux chefs (…) - Coopération

data.title: Cuba perdió 1-3 ante Estados Unidos en su tercera presentación del NORCECA
data.description: El equipo Cuba de Voleibol Masculino cayó este domingo 1-3 ante EE.UU en su tercera presentación del NORCECA, y este lunes enfrentará a Puerto Rico en los cuartos de final. Los cubanos comenzaron ganando el primer set 25-19, pero los estadounidenses reaccionaron y se llevaron los tres parciales siguientes 25-23, 25-18 y 25-14. The post Cuba perdió 1-3 ante Estados Unidos en su tercera presentación del NORCECA first appeared on Cubadebate .

data.title: Espinel explica caída del Olimpia y confiesa: “Este partido no era determinante”
data.description: Tras la derrota 0-1 ante Marathón en el Clásico, el técnico de Olimpia, Eduardo Espinel, lamentó que su equipo no pudiera alcanzar el objetivo de quedarse con los tres puntos, aunque destacó la reacción mostrada pese a jugar con un hombre menos: “La valoración es mucha tristeza porque no conseguimos el objetivo, que era ganar el partido”, expresó el uruguayo, quien además defendió la actitud de sus dirigidos: “Olimpia sigue demostrando que es un equipo que nunca se da por vencido”. Uno de los puntos que Espinel explicó con mayor énfasis fue la rotación del plantel, especialmente por la seguidilla de partidos entre la Liga Nacional y la Copa Centroamericana . El entrenador aseguró que la decisión respondió a una cuestión física y a la necesidad de evitar lesiones: “Las horas de descanso no estaban cumplidas por algunos jugadores”. Y agregó: “Teníamos que apostar a los jugadores que tenían más frescura y no hipotecar el futuro del equipo”, recordando que Olimpia cuenta con un plantel corto. El uruguayo también explicó por qué los Albos terminaron recurriendo al juego directo después de la expulsión y rechazó que los balones largos fueran producto de la desesperación: “Era una estrategia”, afirmó el DT, al señalar que con un jugador menos era difícil encontrar circuitos de pase ante la superioridad numérica de Marathón . Además, restó importancia a la pérdida del invicto y dejó claro cuáles son las prioridades del equipo: “Nuestro objetivo es pelear el campeonato local y el campeonato centroamericano”. ¿Cuál es el análisis que le deja en caliente el final del partido y qué valoración tiene de esa expulsión de Emmanuel Cuello? La valoración es mucha tristeza porque no conseguimos el objetivo, que era ganar el partido. Sabíamos que igual iba a ser un partido difícil, donde veníamos los dos equipos teniendo buena presentación, tanto a nivel local como a nivel internacional, y creo que los detalles terminan definiendo el partido. Y bueno, en cuanto a la expulsión, quedaron con un hombre de menos. Fue un partido muy parejo, donde jugamos contra un rival con el que jugamos bien al fútbol. Nos dificultó un poco ese segundo tiempo, pero hay que rescatar también el esfuerzo de los jugadores, que pese a eso intentaron, fueron al frente y tuvimos ocasiones de poder empatar el partido. Pero bueno, esto es fútbol. Ahora lo que queda es corregir. No hay mucho tiempo: corregir, porque ya mañana hay que trabajar de vuelta. Hay algunas cosas por ahí que no salieron tan bien hoy y que podemos mejorar, pero sabiendo que dimos todo, que dimos todo, aunque no nos alcanzó. Esos últimos 10 minutos intensos hicieron perder el manejo del balón. ¿Esa fue la indicación, que todo fueran balones aéreos y trazos largos para buscar el empate, o fue meramente desesperación del equipo? No, no. Era una estrategia, porque cuando vos te quedás con un hombre de menos, el rival tiene la superioridad numérica. Para tener el balón hay que tener un hombre libre, siempre, mediante los movimientos, y era imposible tener un hombre libre para recibir porque tenía la superioridad numérica. Entonces se apostaba al juego directo y, bueno, cuando no, por supuesto que hay plan A, plan B, plan C. Nunca pensamos, por ejemplo, terminar con 10, pero está previsto que si en algún momento pasaba y no podíamos encontrar la pelota o los circuitos de pases por esa superioridad numérica que el rival tenía, teníamos que saltear líneas. Creo que apostamos un poco a eso. Tuvimos la posibilidad de hacer alguna o rematar alguna jugada de gol, pero bueno, no querían entrar a llevar el balón. Un planteamiento con bastantes rotaciones, teniendo en cuenta que el partido en El Salvador quedó prácticamente liquidado, 3-0 está la serie. ¿Por qué hacen tantas rotaciones, teniendo en cuenta que cualquier jugador de Olimpia está preparado para jugar cualquier tipo de partido? Porque hay un tema físico que hay que respetar. Las horas de descanso no estaban cumplidas por algunos jugadores. Ese es el análisis que hemos hecho desde que llegamos acá. Hace dos años que hemos hecho eso y, por suerte, no hemos tenido lesiones graves y hemos terminado bastante bien en ese sentido. Entonces, más allá de que usted diga que está la serie cerrada y todo eso de la Copa Centroamericana, nosotros no lo entendemos así. Hay que jugar los partidos de fútbol. Tampoco podíamos arriesgar. De hecho, había jugadores en el banco que no estaban para jugar, no estaban para jugar, tenían molestias y dolores. Entonces teníamos que apostar a los jugadores que tenían más frescura y no hipotecar el futuro del equipo. data.translatedTitle: Espinel explica caída del Olimpia y confiesa: “Este partido no era determinante”
data.translatedDescription: Tras la derrota 0-1 ante Marathón en el Clásico, el técnico de Olimpia, Eduardo Espinel, lamentó que su equipo no pudiera alcanzar el objetivo de quedarse con los tres puntos, aunque destacó la reacción mostrada pese a jugar con un hombre menos: “La valoración es mucha tristeza porque no conseguimos el objetivo, que era ganar el partido”, expresó el uruguayo, quien además defendió la actitud de sus dirigidos: “Olimpia sigue demostrando que es un equipo que nunca se da por vencido”. Uno de los puntos que Espinel explicó con mayor énfasis fue la rotación del plantel, especialmente por la seguidilla de partidos entre la Liga Nacional y la Copa Centroamericana . El entrenador aseguró que la decisión respondió a una cuestión física y a la necesidad de evitar lesiones: “Las horas de descanso no estaban cumplidas por algunos jugadores”. Y agregó: “Teníamos que apostar a los jugadores que tenían más frescura y no hipotecar el futuro del equipo”, recordando que Olimpia cuenta con un plantel corto. El uruguayo también explicó por qué los Albos terminaron recurriendo al juego directo después de la expulsión y rechazó que los balones largos fueran producto de la desesperación: “Era una estrategia”, afirmó el DT, al señalar que con un jugador menos era difícil encontrar circuitos de pase ante la superioridad numérica de Marathón .
